title: Regulatory inspection simulation playbook and mock-evidence binder
content:
Purpose:
This is a lightweight, operational playbook to run a simulated regulatory inspection against Redwood Private deployments and region-pinning controls. Primary goals: validate evidence collection, operator scripts, KMS/HSM locational claims, and legal escalation touchpoints. Not intended to be the legal final artifact — use for readiness drills and to harden gaps.

Scope (what we simulate):
- On-prem / VPC customer with region pin enabled (EU anchor)
- Requests and persistent logs for a 30-day window
- KMS key locational metadata and HSM access logs
- Operator responses to a regulator information request and chain-of-custody proofs
- Fallback routing evidence (how traffic was routed during a simulated failover)
- Evidence packaging and redaction steps for PII/PHI concerns

Out-of-scope (for this drill):
- Full legal subpoena responses (legal to run live)
- Cross-border contracts; we only exercise operational attachments

Assumptions / Pre-reqs (check before the drill):
- Customer tenant with pin=eu exists in testbed environment (tenant-id test-geo-003)
- Telemetry retention pipeline in staging keeps 90 days of residency markers
- Operator role accounts (ops-runbook, residency-auditor) created and MFA enforced
- Test KMS keys exist with location labels set to eu-west-1 for the tenant
- A “regulator persona” account is provisioned (mock-regulator@redwood.test)

Roles & responsibilities:
- Run lead: Priya (coordinates timeline, injects scenarios)
- Evidence wrangler: Mateo (packages logs, generates hashes, tracks chain-of-custody)
- Operator responder: Ava (executes runbook steps and communicates with mock-regulator)
- Legal observer: Janelle (notes legal questions, redaction guidance)
- SRE: Rohit (prepares telemetry queries and environment snapshots)

Artifacts we expect to produce (minimum viable evidence):
- System snapshot: model-serving node list, region tags, model versions (timestamped)
- Request lineage: sample request ids, originating IPs, route decisions, and final execution host
- KV/prefix cache evidence: snapshots showing cache population and whether it was seeded outside pinned region
- KMS/HSM audit: key create/rotate/use logs with geo-labels and KMS client ARN mapping
- Operator tickets: timeline of operator interventions and change events (audit trail)
- Telemetry slices: residency flags, sampling traces, and routing decision logs
- Hash manifest + chain-of-custody csv (who accessed what file and when)

High-level timeline (4 hour tabletop run):
- 00:00–00:30: Kickoff, confirm pre-reqs, baseline snapshot (SRE)
- 00:30–01:00: Evidence wrangler extracts sample artifacts; start manifesting hashes
- 01:00–02:00: Regulator persona issues information request — operator to follow scripted response timeline
- 02:00–02:30: Inject an infrastructure failover (simulate EU->fallback region) and capture routing evidence
- 02:30–03:00: Legal observer raises redaction question; operator demonstrates redaction pipeline on a sample
- 03:00–03:30: Collate binder materials and deliver to mock-regulator; time the response
- 03:30–04:00: After-action, list action items, open questions, and risk-scoring

Detailed operator scripts (short form):
- Step O1: Receive regulator request (email template in appendix). Acknowledge within 1 hour.
- Step O2: Lock write access to persistence snapshot (freeze snapshot marker) to ensure reproducible evidence.
- Step O3: Run telemetry queries (prewritten queries saved under infra/telemetry/region-claims) and export CSVs.
- Step O4: Package KMS audit logs using key-id filter; do not include raw secrets or unredacted PII.
- Step O5: Generate SHA256 manifest for each artifact, sign with ops-runbook key, and store manifest in evidence-bucket/test-geo-003/sim-2025-01-07/
- Step O6: Create chain-of-custody document (template in appendix) and add signatures from Evidence wrangler + Run lead.

Mock regulator Q&A (examples we should be able to answer):
- Q: Show proof the tenant’s requests executed on hosts physically in eu-west-1 for window X.
  A: Provide routing logs + node meta, plus signed manifest for snapshot.
- Q: Show KMS key usage for data-at-rest encryption and the key’s control plane location.
  A: Provide KMS audit logs and encryption key metadata; demonstrate HSM-locality label.
- Q: Were any cached items served from outside the region during the window?
  A: Provide KV cache population timeline and TTL eviction events; correlate with route decisions.

Evidence packaging constraints and redaction rules:
- Never include raw request payloads that contain cleartext PII/PHI unless legal signs off. Use redaction pipeline in tools/redact/ and include a redaction log.
- Timestamps must be UTC and include timezone normalization note in binder.
- Sensitive storage keys: reveal only key ids and metadata; do not include private key material.

Failure injection checklist (SRE):
- Prepare a simulated region network partition between eu-west and eu-backup; pre-seed traffic slices for the tenant.
- Verify fallback routing policy triggers and capture decision timeline via tracing hooks.
- Ensure that telemetry events for the fallback include residency-tag and reason-code.

Post-drill analysis (deliverables):
- Action items (triaged by severity) with owners and ETA
- Gap matrix mapping to policy controls (e.g., KMS labeling gaps, telemetry retention gaps)
- Updated runbook snippets (add any query fixes, new artifact locations)
- A small candidate checklist for legal to review and adopt into formal subpoena procedures

Metrics to capture for readiness scoring:
- Evidence assembly time (baseline target: <2 hours)
- Fraction of required artifacts produced without legal help (>90%)
- Number of redaction iterations required (<2)
- Divergence in timestamped snapshots (should be reproducible within 5s for snapshoted items)

Open questions / known blind spots (to track):
- How do we assert HSM physical location for third-party cloud HSM offerings used in some private deployments?
- Do our telemetry retention SLAs cover audit windows for EU regulators in every contracted customer tier?
- Operator experience: can oncall staff generate the manifest and chain-of-custody without dev assistance?

Appendix (quick links & templates):
- A. Regulator acknowledgement email template (ops/templates/regulator_ack.txt)
- B. Chain-of-custody csv template (ops/templates/chain_of_custody.csv)
- C. Sample telemetry queries (infra/telemetry/region_claims_queries.sql)
- D. Evidence manifest signing steps (ops/secrets/signing-notes.md)

Notes to self (informal):
- Run this in staging first with test-geo-003 then try a scaled run with 3 tenants across US/EU/UK.
- Mateo: prepopulate evidence-bucket with dummy manifests to exercise redaction pipeline.
- Bring legal into the loop early; we need a short checklist they own for “can-we-send” decisions.

Next steps (proposed):
- Schedule 2-hour dry run with SRE + ops (target week of 2024-12-02)
- Incorporate feedback into official subpoena-runbook owned by Legal
- Add a nightly cron that validates telemetry queries return expected residency flags for a small sample of tenants (low-cost health check)

End (version notes):
- v0.1 draft by Priya Singh 2024-11-15
- v0.2 updated with SRE checklist and timeline 2024-12-05
- v0.3 added manifest signing steps and mock-regulator template 2025-01-07
